proposed_quote: A 110-kilodalton polypeptide isolated from cell-free culture supernatants of hemolytic Escherichia coli was shown to be associated with hemolytic activity.
notes: Cited ref 10.1128/jb.163.1.94-105.1985 (PMID 3891743, Felmlee/Pellett/Welch 1985) is the hemolysin DNA-sequencing/transcriptional-organization paper; quote is verbatim from its abstract but describes predicted molecular masses, NOT secretion. The companion paper PMID 3891742 (DOI 10.1128/jb.163.1.88-93.1985, same authors, same JB issue) directly documents HlyA extracellular release (culture supernatant). E. coli organism match. Proposed quote verbatim from PMID 3891742 abstract.

DOI 10.1128/jb.172.5.2343-2350.1990 = PMID 2185213 (Highlander/Engler/Weinstock 1990), title "Secretion and expression of the Pasteurella haemolytica Leukotoxin." M. haemolytica (=P. haemolytica) match. Documents secretion via heteroplasmid HlyB/HlyD complementation. Quote verbatim in abstract.

DOI 10.1016/j.gene.2006.10.004 = PMID 17116373 (Crosby/Kachlany 2006, TdeA). A. actinomycetemcomitans match (UniProt P16462 confirmed). Documents secretion: tdeA mutant did not secrete LtxA; TolC-like protein required for LtxA secretion. Quote is a composite of three verbatim spans (joined by ellipses), each appears verbatim in abstract.

proposed_quote: Erwinia chrysanthemi, a phytopathogenic enterobacterium, secretes three proteases (PrtA, PrtB and PrtC) into the extracellular medium.
notes: Cited ref 10.1128/jb.179.15.4754-4760.1997 (PMID 9244262, Akatsuka 1997) demonstrates secretion of the SERRATIA MARCESCENS PrtA via the E. chrysanthemi PrtDEF exporter; quote is verbatim but is about Serratia PrtA homologous to E. chrysanthemi proteases, NOT the E. chrysanthemi PrtA protein (Q07295 = E. chrysanthemi Serralysin A). Correct ref for Q07295 = Ghigo & Wandersman 1992 (PMID 1494344, DOI 10.1007/BF00279652), the prtA cloning/secretion paper cited by UniProt Q07295. Proposed quote verbatim from its abstract; that paper also states "PrtA secretion requires the E. chrysanthemi protease secretion factors PrtD, PrtE and PrtF."

proposed_quote: One of the secreted proteins is PrtA, which is shown here to be a repeats-in-toxin (RTX) alkaline zinc metalloprotease.
notes: DOI 10.1099/mic.0.26171-0 = PMID 12777498 (Bowen et al. 2003) is the correct ref; Photorhabdus luminescens strain W14 (UniProt Q84F70 organism confirmed). Paper documents PrtA secretion. But the cited quote ("The prtA gene resides in a locus encoding both the protease ABC transporter (prtBCD)...") is verbatim yet describes the genetic locus, not secretion. Proposed quote is the verbatim secretion sentence from the same abstract.

DOI 10.1016/S0021-9258(18)81905-6 = PMID 2722818 (Delepelaire & Wandersman 1989, JBC 264:9083), title "Protease secretion by Erwinia chrysanthemi. Proteases B and C are synthesized and secreted as zymogens without a signal peptide." E. chrysanthemi match (UniProt P16316 = Serralysin B). Documents secretion into external medium. Quote is composite of three verbatim spans, each appears verbatim in abstract.

DOI 10.1128/jb.179.15.4754-4760.1997 = PMID 9244262 (Akatsuka 1997). Quote "LipA, HasA, and E. chrysanthemi PrtC were secreted via heterologous exporters and via some hybrid exporters." is verbatim in abstract and explicitly names E. chrysanthemi PrtC (UniProt P16317 = Serralysin C) being secreted. Organism match; documents secretion.

DOI 10.1128/JB.01319-06 = PMID 17098895 (Kehl-Fie & St Geme 2006). Kingella kingae match (UniProt A1YKW7 cites this PMID). Quote is verbatim from abstract but describes genetic identification of an RTX toxin locus via mariner mutagenesis / loss of cytotoxicity, NOT a secretion assay. Accessible text (abstract only; full text empty) documents cytotoxicity/LDH release on host cells and an RTX toxin system locus; secretion as a T1SS substrate rests on RTX-family classification + host-cell cytotoxicity, no direct supernatant/secretion-machinery-dependent export assay shown. Flag for human review.
